newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt says union claim irresponsible.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt says union claim irresponsible.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it had told the Australian Industrial Relations Commission that the Australian Council of Trade Unions' (ACTU) wage claim was irresponsible.
"In the current economic environment, the ACTU's claim is simply irresponsible," Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said in a statement.

The ACTU, Australia's peak union body, has proposed to the commission that all workers not covered by workplace deals get an 8.75 percent increase in award rates and three A$20 a week safety net adjustments over three years.
"It (the claim) is not targeted at the low paid, as the ACTU purports," Reith said. The goverment put its case in an oral submission on Thursday.
"In fact, it will lead to reduced employment for the low paid," he said.
"Based on Treasury estimates, if the commission were to grant all three stages of the ACTU's claim, it is possible there would be as many as 400,000 fewer jobs."
Reith also repeated the government's earlier warning that interest rates could go up if the commission granted the ACTU's claim.

"On the other hand, the government's position of an A$8 per week increase in each of the next three years protects the real value of wages of those on the lowest award classifications and more importantly, doesn't put their jobs at risk," he said.
"It also allows business to plan ahead with some certainty."
